task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
methodological_questions: Does lineup role coverage vary within team across lineups and seasons?
Is role coverage separable from player talent and from role counts, or is it collinear with them?
Does talent control absorb confounding, and does the talent-control specification behave stably?
What sample size, exposure, and reliability constraints apply to lineup-level role measures built from play-by-play possessions?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins. corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. After talent control the adaptation term was not significant (per-series logistic adapt_diff_z p=0.2755; team-in-series cluster adapt p=0.2449), while talent was (p=0.0213 and p=0.0095). Sample was n=55 series. Recorded limitation: confounding and small sample; [prior work] states that n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Reported lineup PPP gaps for named star initiators (for example Jokic vs MIN PPP 0.814, -0.385, n=59; Curry vs HOU 0.851, -0.358, n=47; Doncic vs LAC 0.733, -0.396, n=30). Built on a min-15 gate over 8 play types with opposing DEFENSE_LINEUP coverage of about 84%. No validation recorded.

Series-level AVOID share vs winning. Game-level rho=-0.19, p=0.008, but [prior work] flags inflated n and team-quality confounding. Series-level rho=-0.26, p=0.07 with n=50; [prior work] states about 80 series are needed for p<0.05. Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Sequence-memory lag effects with game-state controls. Naive lag-1 play-type PPP effects were real in naive tests, but DRIVE (ctrl_p=0.0911) and PNR (controlled p=0.136) effects disappeared under game-state controls and within-team baselines. Lag-2 and lag-3+ effects were small or near zero. Verdict recorded as null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a role or adaptation measure against outcomes after controlling for team talent at series level.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as unanswerable: after talent control the adaptation term was not significant, and about 55 series could not separate the coaching signal from roster quality (CONFOUNDING, SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing lineup and forced-play-type suppression to named star initiators without a placebo or matching.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded mechanism is unclear. No placebo or matching was run, and [prior work] notes that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts (PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level AVOID share as a predictor of winning, independent of team quality.
failed_approaches.why: Game-level result was inflated by non-independent observations and team-quality confounding. Series-level result was underpowered (n=50, p=0.07) and recorded as inconclusive (CONFOUNDING, SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive lag-1 play-type PPP effects as evidence of sequence effects.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact: DRIVE and PNR lag-1 effects disappeared with game-state controls and within-team baselines (construction/selection flaw).

evidence_establishes: Talent-adjacent confounding has previously dominated team-level and series-level role or adaptation measures, so any role-coverage effect needs explicit talent control.
Naive play-type or role effects from this project's play-by-play have repeatedly disappeared under game-state and within-team controls, so the same controls are required here.

Series-level samples of about 50 to 55 are recorded as too small to detect modest effects, which supports the concern that a team-season or series-level design would be underpowered for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) directly, so no retrieved record establishes within-team variation in coverage.
No retrieved record shows whether coverage is separable from talent or role counts at lineup-possession level.
No record gives reliability estimates for the role labels or validated talent measures for this data version.
The retrieved records do not show whether talent control behaves stably in lineup-level models.
own_inferences: The 420,993-possession unit is far larger than the series-level units in [prior work], so the power problem recorded for series designs may not carry over to lineup-possession designs. Within-team coverage variation can plausibly be estimated at lineup-stint level.

The 90 team-seasons are the binding constraint for any claim that depends on between-team or talent-level variation, because talent is measured per team-season or per player-season and the number of independent units is small.
Role coverage is likely collinear with talent and with role counts, since starters with high usage tend to supply more roles. Separability therefore has to be tested by decomposition, not assumed.
Role labels are derived from the play-by-play and graph, so any outcome built from the same possessions risks outcome-derived labels and leakage.
uncertainties: The question as posed does not define the role labels, the coverage metric, the talent measure, or the success criterion for 'talent control behaves'.
Reliability of role assignment from play-by-play is unknown.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, and the 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13. Results depend on which data version is used.
Retrieval returned no record testing lineup role coverage, so prior-work coverage is thin and the findings above are analogies, not direct evidence.

historical_effect.explanation: [prior work] show that talent-confounded and series-level designs failed here and that naive play-type effects were artifacts under game-state controls. This moved the decision from a plain test to a proceed-with-changes plan: the unit must be lineup-stint level, talent control must be specified and tested before the coverage claim, and placebo and falsification checks are required. [prior work] did not show that the question is answerable, so the decision is conditional.

blocking_constraints.text: Role coverage is likely collinear with player talent and role counts. Separability must be shown by decomposition before any effect is interpreted, and the talent measure must be defined and validated.
Only 90 team-seasons are available. Any test that depends on between-team or talent-level variation is underpowered, as the series-level records show.
Reliability of role labels from play-by-play is not established, and the question's 'talent control behaves' criterion is not operationalised.
Prior star-lineup results were not validated against placebo, so a placebo or matched comparison is required before any coverage effect is claimed.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) directly. Retrieved records cover related questions: talent-controlled adaptation vs series wins (untestable), star-lineup suppression (not a hypothesis test, no placebo), series-level AVOID share (untestable, inconclusive), and lag effects with game-state controls (artifact). They establish the confounding and power problems and the need for placebo and controls, but do not answer the question.

risks.text: Coverage is likely collinear with talent and role counts; without decomposition, a coverage effect cannot be separated from roster quality, as in [prior work][prior work].
Team-season or series-level talent contrasts have roughly 90 or fewer independent units, below the power needed for modest effects, as in [prior work][prior work].
Some lineups with particular role combinations will have few possessions, so lineup-level cells need a minimum-exposure gate.
Role labels derived from play type and graph may be unreliable; reliability must be estimated before use.
Selecting lineups or teams with extreme coverage may produce regression to the mean; a split-sample or shrinkage design is needed.
Role labels built from the same possessions used to measure points per possession make the outcome partly define the exposure; labels must come from data separate from the outcome.
Possession-level labels must use only information available before the possession; post-hoc play labels leak outcome information.
Coverage of all three roles may be rare, so the base rate of full coverage must be reported before power is assessed.
Star-lineup results without placebo were treated as artifacts in [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work]; a placebo lineup or shuffled-role check is required.
Three roles, several talent specifications, and several seasons create many contrasts; a single pre-specified primary test is needed.
Play-style and rotation patterns change across 2022-23 to 2025-26; season effects must be modelled and not pooled blindly.
Derived play-type records come from a graph built from play-by-play; joins between graph records and per-game files can mis-assign players or possessions.
Partial 2025-26 data before the completion dates must not be mixed with complete data.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal on court) and possession-level points per possession, after conditioning on player-level talent, and the share of coverage variance that is separable from talent and role counts.
design.unit: Lineup stint within team-season (possession-weighted), with possessions nested in stints and stints nested in team-seasons.
design.sample: Complete data only: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season from 2026-04-13. Exclude the partial 2025-26 playoffs before 2026-06-21. Use 420,993 possessions across 90 team-seasons, with a minimum-exposure gate per lineup cell (for example 15 possessions, pre-registered).
design.power: Report the base rate of each role and of full coverage first. Compute power by simulation at the stint level. The 90 team-seasons are the binding constraint for between-team claims; state a minimum detectable within-team effect before running. If the simulated power is low, report the question as exploratory.
design.controls: Player-level talent measured out-of-sample (for example shrunk prior-season net rating or a regularised plus-minus) entered as a control; role counts entered explicitly; game state (period, clock, score margin); opposing lineup strength; minutes; team-season fixed effects. Role labels derived only from information available before each possession (no outcome-derived labels). Estimate reliability of role labels by split-half agreement before use.
design.falsification: Placebo role labels: shuffle role assignments within player across stints and re-estimate; the coverage effect should vanish. Placebo lineups: match lineups on talent and counts and show that the coverage contrast remains null where it should be null. Test whether talent control alone reproduces the coverage effect (it should not). Pre-specified: if the placebo effect is comparable to the observed effect, report artifact.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary contrast (coverage of at least one role vs none, within team, talent-controlled). Secondary contrasts for each individual role and for separability are reported with Holm correction across the listed tests.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if: (a) within-team coverage variance is non-trivial and reliability is adequate; (b) the primary coverage effect survives talent and role-count controls with a 95% interval excluding zero; (c) it exceeds the placebo distribution; (d) it holds in a held-out season and in the playoff subset. Artifact if the placebo matches the observed effect. Uncertain if power is below the pre-stated threshold or reliability fails. Rejected only if the design has adequate power (pre-stated) and the effect interval excludes the pre-specified minimum meaningful effect.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-07-13: complete regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21 (exclude before). Derived play-type graph records built from the same play-by-play.
